entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Theodora of Arta was a Byzantine noblewoman and Orthodox Christian saint canonized in the 14th century for her piety and contributions to the Epirus region. Born into a prominent family, she married into the imperial household and became a revered figure in the local church.

As a patron of the arts and education, Theodora supported the construction of several churches and monasteries throughout Epirus, leaving behind a lasting legacy in the region's architectural heritage. Her emphasis on the importance of women's roles in society also had a profound impact on the development of Orthodox Christian theology.

Theodora's influence extended beyond her local community, with many historians noting her significance as a key figure in the preservation and transmission of Byzantine cultural practices during the tumultuous 14th century. Her legacy continues to inspire art, literature, and scholarship today, ensuring her place as one of the most important female figures in Epirus's medieval history.

In 2018, Theodora Petraliphaina was recognized by the Greek Orthodox Church as a saint, solidifying her status as a revered figure in Orthodox Christian tradition. Her feast day is still celebrated annually in Greece and other parts of the Orthodox world.
